images.title: Every prime twice, or one left alone
images.purpose: Shows 1156 with every prime appearing an even number of times, so 1156 = 34², and 2800 with a single 7, so it is not a square.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Two rows, one above the other, each a number followed by its prime power cards.
images.exact_structure: Top row: the number 1156, then exactly 2 rounded cards filled teal (#0072B2) reading 2² and 17², then = 34² with a small teal (#0072B2) tick mark. Bottom row: the number 2800, then exactly 3 rounded cards: 2⁴ and 5² filled teal (#0072B2), and 7 filled vermilion (#D55E00), then a small vermilion (#D55E00) cross mark. The two rows are left aligned with wide space between them. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A number is a perfect square only when every prime factor appears an even number of times.
images.description: Shows 1156 with every prime appearing an even number of times, so 1156 = 34², and 2800 with a single 7, so it is not a square.

image_decisions.why: The lone 7 shows why ending in two zeros does not make 2800 a square, while 1156 pairs up fully.
